POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd Appoints New Country Head to Bolster Chile Operations

SANTIAGO, June 12 – POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd, a major player in Chile’s engineering and construction sector, announced on Wednesday the appointment of María Ignacia Torres as its new Country Head for Chile, effective immediately. 

The appointment marks a strategic move aimed at strengthening the company’s regional presence amid increasing demand for sustainable infrastructure projects. Torres, who brings over 15 years of experience in large-scale project management across Latin America, will oversee all operational, commercial, and stakeholder engagement activities in the country.

“We are thrilled to welcome Ms. Torres to our team. Her proven leadership and deep understanding of Chile’s evolving infrastructure landscape will be crucial as we continue to support national development priorities,” said Jaehyun Lee, CEO of POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd, in a statement. “Our commitment to sustainable engineering and community partnership remains unwavering, and we believe this appointment will further enhance our local impact.”

The Chilean engineering and construction industry has seen steady growth over the past year, with sectoral investments projected to rise by 5.2% in 2024, according to the Chilean Chamber of Construction. The government’s increased focus on green energy and resilient infrastructure has prompted international firms like POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd to expand their footprint.

Industry analysts have welcomed the appointment. “Bringing in leadership with strong local expertise is a wise move for multinationals operating in Chile,” said Fernando Ríos, a construction sector analyst at Santiago-based consultancy Rivarol Partners. “Given the complexity of new regulatory requirements and the push for sustainable project delivery, this decision positions the company well for upcoming public and private tenders.”

Torres expressed optimism about the company’s prospects. “Chile stands at the cusp of a green infrastructure transformation, and I am honored to lead POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd’s efforts in supporting this transition,” she said during a press conference at the company’s Santiago office. “We are committed to building lasting partnerships with local communities, suppliers, and authorities to deliver innovative solutions that meet the highest environmental and safety standards.”

POSCO Eco & Challenge Co Ltd currently employs more than 400 staff in Chile and is engaged in several major projects, including the construction of renewable energy facilities and water management systems across the country.
